title: First bands, instruments and washboard players
summary: She says bands were not like George's; she names early players, bass and violin, no clarinet, and street washboard and saw players.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Do you have any more questions? I was wondering a little bit more about some of the other dances. If they ever charged admission at any of those halls, could anybody go? Or were there just a certain club would usually give a dance? Anybody, anybody could go, anybody. Anybody could go. Do you remember what kind of bands, when was the first time that you heard a band something like George has now? Was there any old band?
They didn't have no band like that. Nothing like that in their songs? Mm-mm. They had Chiot, Doublet, and old man Jeannot, but it wasn't like it is now.

Well, they played, what you call it, Carmney, and LaBas Plenty. Bass. What you call them, how you call that man just? Albert Glenny. Albert Glenny. Well, he was a bass player. And old man Jeannot was a bass player. They had another bass player. But they didn't play like they play now.
Did they use any clarinets like George plays?
I don't remember any clarinet. I don't remember. La flute, violon, you lit with violin.
Do you remember any homemade instruments or things like washboards and beating on logs? I saw them on the street.
On the street. People used to play. They had a man used to play on Royal Street with washboard and made good music.
When was that? Was that before George was born?
Oh, yes, indeed. Oh, yes. They had a man with a saw and one with a washboard on the Royal Street. We used to play.
